4.1: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 43 — dispositions are innate, natural or acquired; these five sources of power sort the same way. Veda: herbs and mantras are the Atharvaveda’s domain; tapas is the Upaniṣads’ (Taittirīya Up. 3.2); Ṛgveda 10.136 praises the muni with powers. Meaning: Yoga accepts all the Vedic sources of power, but ranks samādhi above the rest (4.6).
4.2: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 16 — prakṛti changes ‘like water’, taking the form of each receptacle; SK 42 — the subtle body takes many forms. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.2.3 — ‘it thought: may I be many’. Meaning: change of form is nature filling a new shape.
4.3: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 31 — the organs act by mutual impulse, puruṣa’s purpose being the only cause; SK 57 — prakṛti flows unprompted, like milk for the calf. The farmer opening a dam, in Vyāsa’s gloss, makes the same point. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.2.15 — ‘by his light all this shines.’ Meaning: causes don’t push nature; they remove what blocks it.
4.4: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 24–25 — from ahaṃkāra come the senses and mind; here the yogi uses asmitā to make whole minds. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 1.4.3 — the Self ‘did not delight alone … it made itself two.’ Meaning: the power of ‘I’ that binds can be used to build.
4.5: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: one directing citta over many, as SK 35 makes buddhi the gatekeeper over the other organs. Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 6.12 — ‘the one controller of the many inactive’. Meaning: many bodies, one directing intelligence.
4.6: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 67 — once knowledge comes, dispositions stop producing new results. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 2.2.8 — ‘his karmas wear away when that is seen’. Meaning: a mind born of meditation leaves no new deposit.
4.7: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 44 — dharma and adharma (white and black) cause ascent and descent; SK 67 — knowledge removes their power. Veda: Īśa Up. 2 — ‘doing works here … karma does not cling to a person’; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.22 — the knower ‘crosses over both’, the good done and the evil done. Meaning: action without self-interest leaves no stain of either colour.
4.8: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 40–42 — the subtle body is ‘perfumed’ (adhivāsita) by dispositions — the same root as vāsanā. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.5 — ‘as is one’s resolve, so the deed; as the deed, so the result.’ Meaning: only those tendencies that fit the present birth wake up.
4.9: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 40 — the subtle body moves through births unchanged in its core. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.3 — like a caterpillar reaching from one blade to the next, the self carries its impressions forward. Meaning: memory and impression bridge any gap of birth, place or time.
4.10: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 52 — dispositions and subtle body need each other; creation has no first moment. Veda: Ṛgveda 10.129.4 — ‘in the beginning desire arose, the first seed of mind.’ Meaning: the will-to-be is as old as the cosmos.
4.11: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: cause, fruit, support and object — remove them and vāsanās vanish, as SK 67 says dispositions lose their causal power. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.14–15 — ‘when all desires of the heart are released … when all knots of the heart are cut.’ Meaning: tendencies are held together by four ties; cut them and they fall.
4.12: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: past and future are real in their own form — SK 9, satkāryavāda. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.2.2 — ‘how could being come from non-being?’ Meaning: what was and what will be are latent now, not nothing.
4.13: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 12–14 — all manifest things are made of the three guṇas. Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 4.5 — the red, white and black unborn one; Atharvaveda 10.8.43 — ‘the lotus covered by three guṇas’. Meaning: everything that appears is a mix of three strands.
4.14: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: a thing’s unity comes from the guṇas acting together, like SK 13’s lamp — wick, oil and flame for one purpose. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.4.1 — in fire, the red is of fire, the white of water, the black of food. Meaning: one thing is a coordinated change of three.
4.15: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 11 — the manifest is ‘objective’ (viṣaya) and ‘common’ (sāmānya), shared by all. So the object and the mind run on different tracks. Veda: here Yoga parts from later Vedānta readings — Chāndogya Up. 6.2.1 calls what is ‘being (sat)’, and Yoga takes the world’s being at its word rather than calling it the mind’s projection. Meaning: different minds see one object differently, but the object is not their invention.
4.16: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: realism again — SK 11’s ‘common’ objects do not depend on one perceiver. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.2.2 — ‘how could being come from non-being?’ — the world is grounded in being, not in a perceiver. Meaning: the world does not disappear when one stops looking.
4.17: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: buddhi knows only what colours it — SK 36: the organs, like a lamp, light up what is before them. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.3.6 — ‘by what light does a person act?’ Meaning: knowing depends on contact between mind and object.
4.18: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 19 — puruṣa is the unchanging witness of buddhi’s changes. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 3.7.23 — ‘the unseen seer, the unheard hearer’; Kena Up. 1.2 — ‘the mind of the mind’. Meaning: the mind is always known, because its knower never changes.
4.19: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 20 — buddhi is non-conscious (acetana) and only seems conscious. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.2.15 — ‘there the sun does not shine … by his light all this shines.’ Meaning: the mind is lit, not a light.
4.20: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 30 says the inner organs can act ‘together or in sequence’ on an object, but never as seer of themselves. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 3.4.2 — ‘you cannot see the seer of seeing.’ Meaning: the mind cannot be its own witness.
4.21: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 17 — there must be a final enjoyer; otherwise each witness needs another. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 2.4.14 — ‘by what would one know the knower?’ Meaning: the regress stops in the puruṣa.
4.22: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 20 — through conjunction buddhi seems conscious; here consciousness, unmoving, takes buddhi’s form. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 3.1.1 — the watching bird does not eat. Meaning: we know ourselves by reflection in the mind, not by the mind becoming aware.
4.23: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 35 — buddhi, with ahaṃkāra and manas, takes in every object; it faces the seer on one side and the seen on the other. Veda: Maitrī Up. 6.34 — ‘the mind alone is saṃsāra; purify it with effort.’ Meaning: the mind is the meeting place, so it can show everything.
4.24: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 17 almost verbatim — ‘because compounds exist for another (saṃghāta-parārthatvāt)’. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 2.4.5 — ‘all is dear for the sake of the Self.’ Meaning: however rich the mind, it works for someone else.
4.25: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 64 — ‘I am not, nothing is mine, no I’: the end of speculation about who one is. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.22 — ‘not this, not this’. Meaning: for the one who sees the difference, the question ‘what am I?’ stops.
4.26: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 37 — buddhi itself now discerns; it is drawn toward isolation. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.2.1–2 — the wise choose the good. Meaning: the mind that once ran outward now leans toward freedom.
4.27: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 67 — the wheel keeps turning a little from its old impetus. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.14.2 — ‘there is delay only until I am released.’ Meaning: old impressions still arise for a while.
4.28: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: same treatment as the kleśas (2.10–11) — dissolve the subtle, meditate away the active. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.13 — merge inward stage by stage. Meaning: there is nothing new to do, only finishing.
4.29: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: no interest even in the reward of knowledge — SK 66’s indifference. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 3.2.2 — one whose desires are fulfilled. Meaning: the ‘cloud of dharma’ comes when nothing more is wanted.
4.30: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 67 — knowledge removes the causal power of dharma and the rest. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 2.2.8 — ‘the knot of the heart is cut … karmas wear away’; Gītā 4.37 — ‘the fire of knowledge burns all karma to ash.’ Meaning: afflictions and karma end together.
4.31: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 64 — knowledge that is complete and pure. Veda: Īśa Up. 15 — the golden lid removed; Muṇḍaka Up. 2.2.9 — ‘in the highest golden sheath is Brahman, stainless, partless.’ Meaning: once the covering is gone, what remains to know is very little.
4.32: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 59 — the dancer stops after showing herself; SK 66 — ‘I have been seen,’ she ceases. Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 4.5 — the other unborn one leaves her, having enjoyed. Meaning: the guṇas stop changing for one whose purpose is done.
4.33: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: sequence is known only at the end of change — SK 9’s view of change seen from its finish. Veda: Kena Up. 4.4 — ‘the blink of an eye’. Meaning: time is a sequence of moments, seen whole only when it ends.
4.34: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 68 — ‘prakṛti ceases, her purpose done; puruṣa attains absolute and final isolation.’ Patañjali gives the same ending in two forms: the guṇas returning to source, or consciousness in its own nature. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 3.2.8 — ‘as rivers flowing into the ocean lose name and form’; Śvetāśvatara Up. 6.13 — ‘that cause, reached by Sāṃkhya and Yoga — knowing it, one is freed from all bonds.’ Meaning: the Upaniṣad’s promise is what both texts fulfil.
